title: Someone Is Making One of Baldur's Gate 3's Most Popular Villains Romanceable
summary: One of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash, could be romanceable soon thanks to this new fan-made mod.
content: Baldur's Gate 3 has no shortage of romances and romantic encounters, but not everyone in Faerûn is up for a smooch. When developer Larian was still rolling out updates, fans would often ask for more romances to be added, whether it be for Jaheira or Rolan, but it was never meant to be. One of the most popular requests was actually for one of Baldur's Gate 3's main villains, Gortash. Larian was very much aware of this, and actually addressed these fans in the patch notes in 2024. "Listen, he’s a complicated guy who’s busy contemplating the minutia of death cult office politics," Larian said at the time. "Babygurl doesn’t have time to kiss." But now, a fan is stepping up, adding the Gortash romance that so many were asking for. TikTok user Equipouet has shared some clips from the mod, which is still a work in progress. It shows the player character being invited to spend time with Gortash, played by Lucius Malfoy actor Jason Isaacs, after his coronation in Act 3, all with new dialogue and animations. We're told that we'll be able to make our own choices when we meet Gortash, specifically whether we want to "charm him, keep him guessing, or walk away." So, if you really hate Gortash, you could also use the mod to let him down. Much more is teased for the mod, like a ball held by Gortash, letters to exchange with him, and "choices with consequences." There will also be changes to how the story plays out if your character is The Dark Urge, since it's in your backstory that you already have a history with Gortash. The mod is still being worked on, but the author says they will submit it for console release approval once it's done. That process can be lengthy, however, and there's no guarantee that it will pass the approval stage, especially if it's too bulky for console. In the meantime, Gortash kissers will keep having to use their imagination. Like us would-be Jaheira kissers. There are also plenty of other mods to try out, including a bunch that have Larian's seal of approval and can be installed within the game's own mod manager. Image credit: Larian.

title: BioWare Fans Hit Out at EA for Selling New Dragon Age Merch After Killing the Studio
summary: A new Dragon Age hoodie is available on the BioWare Gear store, as EA continues to sell merch based on BioWare's now dead franchises.
content: EA's decision to shut down BioWare sparked a mix of shock and sadness across the internet , with both fans and developers fondly remembering the many role-playing games the Canadian studio put out over the years. The Mass Effect community has been especially vocal , given that Mass Effect 5 was cancelled alongside the studio closure . But Dragon Age fans certainly aren't happy either, and they're making it known. Despite BioWare's closure, the BioWare Gear merch store is still being updated. A bunch of new items were added for N7 Day , but we just got a new Dragon Age merch drop too. For example, the Dragon Age Inquisition Seven of Swords Nightmare Hoodie features a piece of tarot card art that appears in Dragon Age: Inquisition. Better still, the art depicts fan-favourite character Duncan from Dragon Age: Origins. But given that we're only getting this hoodie after everyone who worked on the Dragon Age series lost their job, it isn't sitting well with fans. "Do not give #EA the privilege of royalties on IP they have killed, and will not sell or forfeit," one fan said . "If you want your voice heard and want to #SaveDragonAge and #SaveMassEffect, EA needs to reckon with the consequences of their bad financial decisions. #BoycottEA and licensed merch." "Save Mass Effect. Save Dragon Age. Dragon Age was failed massively by EA. You destroyed what Veilguard could have/should have been because you pushed for it to be live service then backtracked. You never gave Dragon Age the chance it deserved," another person replied to the BioWare Gear Store's post promoting the hoodie . "No studio, No Game = No money," Olarcadia said on X / Twitter . "What you're doing is a pure lack of respect." "It's so cute how you think putting out merch is going to make us hate you any less," onedcdame agreed. "Keep it. BioWare is closed, we're not giving you any of our money EA," replied SignWithBlood. "You should offer to sell back the IP to the founders, including the BioWare brand and name," added @inkpot__gods. "We bought merch to support the devs who made the games we loved; you fired all the devs and stopped making those games, so there’s no one left for us to financially support," said LouEaglesham. It appears that the community plans to boycott EA's continued use of BioWare's IPs, at least until it allows a team of devs to make a new game in these universes. Right now, both Dragon Age and Mass Effect are on ice. Dragon Age fans in particular have a lot to be upset about. The last game in the series, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, largely failed to impress the community. But it has long been known that the game languished in development hell and suffered from various changes in direction. Former BioWare executive producer Mark Darrah recently shared the original vision for the fourth Dragon Age game , before EA allegedly mandated that it had to be a live service. EA would then go on to allow the game to be retooled as a single-player RPG, but The Veilguard had to be built from the bones of this live service work, meaning the developers didn't have time to return to this original outline. It remains to be seen what EA does next with the Dragon Age series. EA is not in the habit of selling off IP, but if enough fans are boycotting the merch, it leaves EA without much to do other than just sit on it.

title: Amazon Has Restocked Loads of Pokémon Cards for Black Friday
summary: Shop Amazon’s best Black Friday Pokémon TCG deals and restocks, including 30th Celebration collections, Booster Bundles, Elite Trainer Boxes and tins.
content: With Pokémon cards being particularly difficult to get hold of throughout the TCG's 30th anniversary year, Amazon has come through with a fresh batch of stock for Black Friday — including some of the more recent releases that you can buy both directly from the retailer and third-party sellers. Amongst the highlights are the very in-demand 30th Celebration Tech Sticker Collection for just $43.95 , the recently released Mega Forces Tin for $35.16 (30% off) , and a handful of other collections for under $50. There are quite a few Booster Bundles available again, as well, if you don't mind buying from other sellers on Amazon's storefront. Black Friday Pokémon TCG Restocks Sold and Shipped by Amazon Of the Pokémon TCG products Amazon itself has in stock, the Mega Forces Tin is one of the best deals to go for this Black Friday. Down from $49.99, you're getting four booster packs alongside a foil promo card of either Mega Dragonite ex, Mega Darkrai ex, or Mega Zeraora ex — with the Dragonite tin alone currently carrying a market value of $55.31 on TCGplayer . Alternatively, the 2026 Deck Crafter's Collection is going for only $11.39 (33% off), including a Meowth ex card, 39 Trainer cards, and a booster pack (Pitch Black from what we’ve seen in the product imagery). Amazon is also advertising a four-for-the-price-of-three promotion — including Magic: The Gathering, Disney Lorcana TCG, and KPop Demon Hunters Collectible Trading Cards — meaning you could save even more. Along with the aforementioned 30th Celebration Tech Sticker Collection, the Unova Poster Collection ($43.72) , Hop's Zacian ex Box ($45.41) , and 2024 World Championships Deck ($35.61) are all available directly from Amazon, too. More Pokémon TCG Black Friday Restocks with Amazon third-party sellers If you're specifically after Booster Bundles, the closest to market price amongst those we've compared is the six-pack Delta Reign box for $47.88 — only $3.94 above TCGplayer’s estimation of $43.93 . There are also Pitch Black and Chaos Rising Booster Bundles for $46.99 and $49.99 respectively, whilst Journey Together can be bought for as little as $52.95 . For collectors after something with a few more extras, there's the First Partner Illustration Collection – Series 3 for $33.99 , Mega Moonlit Tins from $40 , and the 30th Celebration Poster Collection for $43.95 (sold by Kings Games, but shipped by Amazon). Even the Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box can be picked up for under $100, at $97.95 , although that's $18.81 above its $79.14 market price. If you’re the type of trading card collector who doesn’t want to buy anything not shipped by Amazon, be sure to check the specifics of each listing; many third-party listings are indeed still delivered by Amazon despite not being the specific seller, but other third-party sellers ship it themselves.

title: Despite Take-Two Takedown, Vibecoding Teen Behind Nuked GTA 6 PC Port Project 'Leonida' Vows to Continue
summary: The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company.
content: The 15-year-old vibecoder behind a GTA 6 PC port project Take-Two recently shut down has vowed to continue their work despite the potential for further action from the company. ‘NotRexed’ is behind ‘Project Leonida,’ which was at one point leading the race to create a PC port of GTA 6 following the recent leak of an Xbox build. Cyberleek, the infamous leaker behind many early GTA 6 gameplay clips, reportedly released the Xbox build of GTA 6 last week, and vibecoders have been attempting to port the game to PC since. Fueled by AI, progress has been swift, with clips showing GTA 6 running on PC at a higher frame rate than on console, and one video even showing basic multiplayer. Obviously, Rockstar Games, which will no doubt release GTA 6 on PC officially at some point, and parent company Take-Two will be watching the homebrew scene’s every move like a hawk. In the case of Project Leonida, Take-Two has already taken action. NotRexed was organizing and sharing work on a Discord group, and hosting their findings on a GitHub repository, when cease and desists from Take-Two hauled everything offline. NotRexed then took to social media to announce they'd decided to call it a day. “I quit guys. I’m sorry,” NotRexed said. “I really want to make cool stuff but every single time s**t happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the Discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.” NotRexed went on to insist that they were finding it tough to run Project Leonida while also going to school. “Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15-year-old kid,” they said. “Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.” However, NotRexed has now returned, and promised to continue the project. “Ignore my other posts,” NotRexed said after changing their mind. “Something’s coming soon. Leonida is NOT dead. I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I’ll have some stuff to show all of you soon.” IGN spoke to NotRexed to find out why they’re doing this, whether they understand the risks, what they’ll do if they get in legal trouble, and what their parents think of it all. “It’s just a hobby of mine,” NotRexed said in a private message. “I started doing similar things with porting games to the web back in the start of 2026, and I’ve always just thought of it to be cool.” Before generative AI, NotRexed had no interest in porting games to other platforms, they said. But after finding out it was possible in 2025, they’re now taking on one of the most powerful publishers in video games. Interestingly, there’s no real motive behind it. “I’ve always been interested in tech and mess around with it a lot,” they said. According to them, even their parents are aware of what they do and are largely supportive of it. “Yes, they know about all my projects and work I do, and they’re pretty encouraging about it,” they claimed. It made me wonder if they were fully aware of the legal risks involved in such an undertaking. “Yea, they have warned me about what could happen,” NotRexed insisted when I asked if their parents knew about the potential legal issues. “I’m still continuing my work as of now tho because even tho T2 took down my repo and Discord they have never sent an email or message directly to me. If I do get into legal trouble I’m probably gonna stop working on it but possibly have a friend continue it.” How feasible is this? IGN asked Matt Freedman, a veteran game developer with expertise in both traditional development and the controversial emerging technology of AI. “A recompilation is different from a port,” Freedman said. “But yes, an AI driven recompilation of GTA 6 is very doable and wouldn't have the same 'game feel' problems that an AI-driven port would have.” He went on to explain the differences between decompilations, recompilations, and ports. A decomp is where someone manually reverse engineers a game to run on other systems, like the Mario 64 PC port. “This is very time consuming and requires a human to do the work and effectively 'guess' how the game works,” he said. A port takes existing assets or creates new ones and essentially builds a new version of the same game to work on another system. The Witcher 3’s Switch port is an example of this. “A team took The Witcher 3 code base and assets and then modified them by hand to work on the Switch,” he said. For recomps, people use large language models (LLMs) to break down a game and rebuild it, essentially reverse engineering the title for whatever system the user wants. “Since LLMs natively can read binary, they're able to understand the specific code better than humans can,” Freedman explained. A decomp or port of GTA 6 would not be easy — not least because Rockstar uses proprietary tech, including its in-house Rage engine, to power its games. “When it comes to AI, it'll depend on how well it has previously seen the engine or the low level SDK,” Freedman replied when asked about this complication. “A well studied proprietary engine with lots of public information would be easier for it to understand. A custom engine for an obscure CPU would be much more difficult for it. “So, something like Rockstar's Rage engine would be more difficult for it to figure out than something like a game made in Unreal. But… given that a 15-year-old was able to have an AI port GTA 6 to PC, it's clearly not the biggest lift out there.” All the while, Take-Two is working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port appears close to the finish line. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scene uses AI to speed along development. It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports. Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version. Here’s the exchange: IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it? Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended. IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games? Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected. During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up. “This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations. “That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

title: Hollow Knight: Silksong Cherry Time! Special Presentation Reveals Expansion Release Date
summary: Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry is set to issue a long-awaited update on expansion Sea of Sorrow during a Direct-style special presentation today, and IGN is reporting live.
content: Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry's Cherry Time! Special Presentation wrapped up with a release date for expansion Sea of Sorrow. It's free for all players from December 11. The trailer is below: And if you need a catch up on the presentation, check out our live blog!

title: Former Gran Turismo World Series Competitor Helped Tune GTA 6 Car Physics
summary: A former Gran Turismo World Series competitor helped Rockstar tune GTA 6's car physics.
content: A lot of people have complained about the Ganado, Jason’s starting car in GTA 6 , for being tricky to drive. The small pickup is a little unwieldy and prone to swinging out at the back end because it’s based on the Ford Ranchero, a rear-wheel drive whip manufactured between 1957–1979 in North America. While there are no licensed vehicles in GTA 6, cars are recognisable based on real-world counterparts, with small visual changes to make them legally distinct. But the accuracy doesn’t stop at the car model — it also extends to how they drive. That variety in handling is in part because Rockstar hired Lewis Bentley, a former Gran Turismo World Series competitor, to work on the vehicle physics team. Bentley announced the news in a now-deleted YouTube video. “We put the auto in the Grand Theft Auto,” he said from the driver’s seat of his Lotus Elise. Bentley is best known for qualifying for the final in the GT Sport World Tour event at the Nürburgring 24 Hours, in 2018. “Everyone on the physics team’s amazing,” he said in the same video. He claimed to have worked on GTA 6 for around three years in total, and is listed in the game’s credits as a developer in the physics department. Bentley isn’t the only gearhead who worked on the game, however. Rockstar North has its own in-house racing team , and they’re pretty good on the track — they won a team-based 24h Nürburgring event back in 2022. You can see this attention to detail in the game, both in vehicle handling models on cars and on the tracks. For the first time in the series, GTA 6 features a closed asphalt circuit called Gellhorn International Raceway, which stitches together a bunch of iconic corners and racing lines from some of the most famous real-world tracks in existence, turning them into the ultimate speedway. We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 5 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. Just getting started in Chapter 1 ? Check out our Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , and make a note of the Best Free Weapons to Find Early . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

title: PS5 Hit Ghost of Yotei Drops to an All-Time Low In PlayStation’s Black Friday Sale
summary: Ghost of Yotei on PS5 has been discounted to $35 as part of PlayStation's Black Friday sale, making for a 50% discount off its original MSRP and its lowest price yet.
content: Been waiting to play Ghost of Yotei? We've got some good news. PlayStation's Black Friday sale is in full swing now, offering savings on physical games, controllers , and digital game deals . And, if you've missed out so far on the follow up to Ghost of Tsushima, there's a whopping 50% discount on Ghost of Yōtei . Save 50% on Ghost of Yotei In PlayStation’s Black Friday Sale The physical copy is currently on sale for $35 as part of the sale, which is a huge drop from its original $69.99 MSRP and marks a brand new all-time low price for the game, according to our research. That's a pretty great Black Friday deal to have pop up, especially considering the game is only a year old. If you've been eager to pick it up for your PS5 library, now is the perfect time to strike. It's certainly worth the cost, especially in the eyes of our reviewer , Michael Higham. Back when it was released, he gave the game an 8/10 and said that it features a "predictable but well-executed story" that "takes you through Ghost of Yotei's gorgeous landscapes and satisfying, fluid action combat." I managed to play through it earlier this year as well and certainly agree with Michael's thoughts here. If you enjoyed Tsushima, you're sure to have a blast running around in Yōtei, and the combat may actually be even better than its predecessor. It's not just Atsu's adventure seeing discounts in PlayStation's Black Friday sale, either. 2026 launches like Marvel's Wolverine has dropped to $50 as part of the sale, and Saros has also seen a big drop - ideal for anyone looking for a spiritual successor to Returnal. There's also a solid selection of PS5 exclusives on sale for $30 or less right now, including big, beloved titles like God of War Ragnarok, Stellar Blade, and even Ghost of Tsushima (if you want to play Yōtei's predecessor).

title: Hollow Knight: Silksong - Sea of Sorrow Launch Trailer Finally Confirms Release Date, Teases Fishing
summary: Team Cherry's latest showcase gives us a release date for Sea of Sorrow, the free DLC expansion coming to Hollow Knight: Silksong, and a launch trailer.
content: Team Cherry has just wrapped up its Cherry Time! showcase, giving us some long-awaited news on the future of Hollow Knight: Silksong. The big takeaway here is that Hollow Knight: Silksong's first big expansion, Sea of Sorrow, finally has a release date of December 11. Sea of Sorrow will be available to all Silksong players for free. All you need is a copy of the base game, and you can start playing Sea of Sorrow when it goes live on December 11. This also means Team Cherry has stuck to its promise to get Sea of Sorrow out by the end of the year. Some had feared that today's announcement would be a delay — or an announcement that the DLC was being expanded into a full game, which is famously how Silksong's development began. In the showcase, we got a new look at Sea of Sorrow's gameplay. This gives us a good preview of what's in store for us, as we see new areas, enemies, and boss fights. Of course, it all looks as challenging as ever, as you'd expect for Silksong's post-launch DLC. And is that a fishing mini-game teased at the end? We weren't told anything else about the future of Silksong or the Hollow Knight series at large. There was no mention of this being Silksong's only expansion, so it's very possible that Team Cherry plans to support the game beyond Sea of Sorrow. For now, here's the official blurb on Sea of Sorrow: In Sea of Sorrow, players will voyage above and beneath Pharloom’s forgotten ocean, across islands, through forts and into deep caverns beneath the waves. We’ve spent the whole year stuffing this adventure full with all the things you’d expect from Hollow Knight: Silksong - crazed characters, high adventure, and epic bosses! It’s also overflowing with more exceptional music by the eternally talented Christopher Larkin! We’re pretty darn excited to get it into all of your hands on December 11, so please look forward to it. Outside of this reveal, Team Cherry used the attention to promote indie games from other studios. Three were shown off: Blockan and the Walking City, which is fully hand-drawn; Radio Rain, which is centred around 1980s-inspired music; and The Botanist and the Translator, which boasts a Sailor Moon-esque vibe. In a follow-up blog post , Team Cherry confirmed that these new games will release under the new Team Cherry Presents label, which is headed up by the indie developer's fourth team member, Huy Le. Huy is technical director and on-going support for all the Team Cherry Presents games, but has also helped out on Silksong and Sea of Sorrow. "As a long-time team of three people, adding a fourth member is a big deal!" Team Cherry said.

title: I Tried to Get Six Stars in GTA 6 With Just One Bullet and Broke the Game
summary: We tried to get six stars in GTA 6 by firing just one bullet and broke the game.
content: If reaching a six-star wanted level in Grand Theft Auto 6 is your goal, there are many different methods available to you. Raiding the military base for a tank is one way. Committing a horrifying beach massacre is another. But can you get there by firing just a single bullet? We at IGN had a theory that this was absolutely possible, and so spent hours in a fast food joint to find out. When we say “by firing a single bullet,” we mean that technically speaking. Our theory is that your chosen character only needs to pull the trigger once. That’s because, when roaming around GTA 6’s open world and causing whatever brand of chaos you’ve chosen to, your partner will automatically take up the fight against aggressors, and is both invulnerable and stocked with unlimited ammunition. That means if you decide to walk into a heavily populated area as a couple and fire just one bullet into the crowd, your better half can commit the lion's share of the atrocities themselves, provided you just stay alive. We tested this out for ourselves, leading Jason and Lucia to the Taco Bomb in Gellhorn as our chosen arena of violence. Taking control of Jason, one bullet was fired into a poor staff member taking a break outside. Bits of brain now covered the forecourt, which somehow still looked like a more appetising alternative to whatever the questionable-looking beef was they were offering inside. Creeping cannibalistic thoughts pushed to one side, we walked back inside knowing our work was done. This public execution, perhaps rightfully, attracted a police patrol car to the restaurant, of which Lucia did not take kindly to their arrival. Her love for Jason knows no bounds, up to and including unloading full machine gun magazines into any cops who want to arrest him. And who were we to stand in her way? Letting her take control of the situation was then required, honorably moving Jason behind the indestructible cover of an industrial refrigerator. Sporting an armoured vest just in case any stray bullets or shrapnel found their way around the corner, it was then time to hunker down in the kitchen beside that thick metal fridge, out of view of law enforcement. Crucially, this fast food establishment’s kitchen does not have a door leading outside, meaning the threat of flanking cops was neutralised. Luckily, they didn’t seem to spot the drive-thru window, which would’ve handed them a clean shot. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet? And there we sat for a good 45 minutes as Lucia angrily gunned down anyone brave enough to step into the restaurant. No more food would be served today, only death. The red of discarded hot sauce packets replaced by the blood of the fallen. The crunch of hard shell tacos drowned out by the crack of broken bones. All in the name of science. Could a six-star wanted level be achieved by us, the player, firing just one bullet? Well, not this time. We could’ve sat here forever, bravely hiding behind a fridge while our partner slaughtered hundreds. Lucia was invincible, rounds of ammunition sinking into her skin to no effect. She had no shortage of ammo herself; with an unlimited pool of lead to reload from, she could’ve done this all day, and all for us. If that isn’t true romance, I don’t know what is. Day turned to night, and the restaurant workers diligently remained kneeling behind the counter and cowering for the whole sordid ordeal. The problem is, our aggressors just… stopped. After a period of quiet, we chose to break cover and wander outside, only to be met by several non-aggravated members of law enforcement staring blankly at us. We had seemingly confused them with our methods of madness. Because we’re so dedicated to the cause here at IGN, we tried all over again. Putting this first attempt down as an unfortunate glitch, we reloaded a save, made our way to Taco Bomb, and fired a single gunshot into our chosen test subject. And so, another hour of hiding behind a fridge commenced while our incredibly committed girlfriend peppered anyone who dared approach us with bullets. Armoured trucks eventually surrounded the exits, and the sound of helicopter blades could be heard above. But the same thing happened again. We even waited long enough for the rest mode settings on our PS5 to almost put the console to sleep. Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? It seems GTA 6 gets very confused if you decide to start a chain reaction like this, only to go passive for the next 60 minutes. Again, five stars were secured on the wanted level, but that sixth just wouldn’t arrive. The enemy AI’s brain could not comprehend what was happening, so we decided we simply had to intervene. If that sixth star was going to be ours, we’d need to get involved ourselves. Thus, we thought we’d honor the place we’d called home for the past couple of hours, and end our occupancy of Taco Bomb with an explosion. A bunch of incapacitated, but not dead, cops lay writhing on the floor of the restaurant. Could just one grenade be our key to maxing out the wanted level? There was only one way of finding out. We ended the whole bloody affair with a bang, ripping the pin out of the explosive before hurling it into the mound of bodies. And that’s when it happened. Nirvana. The gates of heaven opened. Six-star paradise was ours to bask in. So, what was the point of all of this? Well, more than anything, to confirm that you never have to worry about Jason or Lucia dying when roaming around GTA 6’s open world when not controlling them. Unlike in missions, where they can slip off this mortal coil, they can’t die in free-roam, and so you are clear to use them as superpowered distractions or unkillable meat shields if you wish. You don’t have to be as cowardly as we were, but if you have an hour free to watch an action movie scene play out while peeking out from behind the corner of a refrigerator, then that option is available to you. There are certainly quicker ways to reach GTA 6’s highest wanted level of six stars, which means you’ll be hunted down until you’re dead, but this is one of the safest and requires minimal munitions from your own stockpile. Early on, we opted for the plane crash onto a beach, before mowing down all of the vacationers in a truck method, but since then, millions of players have been finding their own road to infamy. But, in case you ever needed to know. Yes, it is possible to get six stars in GTA 6 with just a single bullet and grenade. As for just the single bullet itself… well, we’ll keep on trying. What have been your wildest six-star stories? Let us know in the comments! title: It Turns Out Jason Might Have a History With Mandy in GTA 6 After All
summary: Mandy is obsessed with Jason in GTA 6, but there's dialogue that suggests they hooked up at least once.
content: As soon as GTA 6 was in our hands, an early game character quickly became a fan favourite: Mandy. Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow. It's not hard to see why. Mandy certainly knows how to make an entrance, as she tries in vain to entice Jason away from Lucia . But alas, it is not meant to be. Fans then did a little digging and found out that Mandy is almost definitely hiding a dark secret ; she's probably killed people. That makes her advances towards Jason — like insisting they were supposed to be married — look dangerously delusional. Jason might have dodged a literal bullet. However, there is some easy-to-miss dialogue in GTA 6 that suggests Mandy wasn't basing her infatuation with Jason on nothing. You can come across this dialogue as soon as you take control of Lucia and find a meditation spot . The meditation sequence will play some audio from the character's past, usually centred around their insecurities. AAAAAAAAAH https://t.co/4xxj8rHZAR — 𐔌 . ⋮ ιvσɾყ ֹ ₊ ꒱ (@ivysmores) November 25, 2026 In one of Lucia's medititation sequences, she recounts a conversation with Jason that she must have had off-screen after they got back in touch. "Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago," we can hear Jason say in Lucia's thoughts. "You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again." Of course, Jason doesn't mention Mandy by name here, but the wording makes it pretty clear it's her. Jason mentions not letting Lucia go again, so it would be after their initial breakup. That means the conversation likely happened after she was released from prison, meaning Lucia was living in the same neighbourhood as Mandy — and was aware of how obsessed she was with Jason. In fact, another easy-to-miss scene does show that Lucia knows about Mandy. At the end of Chapter 1, during the sequence when you're running away from Jason's house as Lucia, you can find Mandy giving a statement to the cops (and, of course, exaggerating how close she was with Jason). This game really has everything lol — Never break kayfabe (@Quadripolar_B) November 25, 2026 If you come out of hiding, Lucia can finally confront Mandy, saying, "Stay the f**k away from Jason, you crazy b*tch." Better yet, the encounter gives us another clue that Mandy is a killer, as she tells the police she "wanted to light [Jason's] house on fire so many times." With all of this in mind, it's no wonder that Jason was eager to stay away from Mandy early on in GTA 6 — it doesn't seem that she understood he wasn't looking for anything long term with her. Luckily for him, it sounds like Lucia is ready to run to his defence. Mandy went viral pretty much as soon as GTA 6 came out, with countless social media posts discussing the character's motivations. Mandy actress Lexie Shoaibi has spoken out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame , pointing out that people keep trying to impersonate her on social media. Shoaibi has also revealed she spent around 10 days on set playing Mandy, but she also did a few other NPC voices while working with Rockstar. title: Losing Six Stars in GTA 6 Is Meant to Be Impossible, but Players Are Trying Everything From Interdimensional Portals to Hidden Bunkers
summary: Losing six stars in GTA 6 is meant to be impossible, but players are trying everything from interdimensional portals to hidden bunkers to escape the cops.
content: GTA 6 's new police system is one of the most interesting things about the game. Instead of omnipresent cops, the police have have various levels of awareness, and you can use guile and cunning to outsmart them and escape. There are still wanted stars, which represent how much of the police force is dedicated to hunting you down, but a well-considered escape plan can get you out of most kinds of trouble. Just escape the search zone, lose line of sight, and change how you look to get away. That is unless you cause too much carnage. If you go off the deep end and cause real mayhem, you’ll eventually reach six stars. Six stars in GTA 6 sees almost the entire map become a search zone, and the cops will never stop tracking you down, according to Rockstar. If you need a pointer, here's how to get a six-star wanted level in GTA 6 . If you hide indoors, the army comes along with a tank. If you jump in a plane, jets are scrambled to shoot you down. If you try to escape by car, attack helicopters perform a strafing run to blow you off the road. Eventually, no matter how hard you try, you will succumb to the pressure. Six stars, it is thought, amounts to a death sentence. But is that guaranteed? Since GTA 6 came out, players have been looking for creative ways of breaking the rule around the highest wanted level. Using clever tricks, some are exploring ways to escape a six-star police hunt and return to regular gameplay — which should technically only be possible two ways: you die or get busted. Warning! GTA 6 spoilers follow. How to lose six-star wanted level in GTA 6 One player used a series of secret bunkers that you can open up to get access to a GTA 6 tank . Here’s the clip: ⭐️ LE PREMIER JOUEUR AU MONDE A RÉUSSIR À SEMER LES 6 ETOILES SUR GTA 6 ! Il est allé dans un sous sol rempli de bunkers pour réussir à semer la police. https://t.co/8Q0nd27eOn — La Twitchance (@LaTwitchance) November 25, 2026 Another player in the comments said they managed to replicate this by swimming. “Bro, I actually did it yesterday. I managed to escape the 6-star wanted level,” they said . “Just keep diving underwater, and when your oxygen is almost depleted, swim back to the surface. Keep repeating this until you find a jet ski. Then ride it beyond the 6-star search area, and boom! You're free.” Some players think the underwater cave system in Emerald Springs could be another prime candidate, since cops can’t send diving teams after you. If you head to Emerald Spring and look for signs for the Selkie Hole, there’s diving equipment you can use to explore an underground cave network. Another player went to more extreme lengths to avoid the cops. After completing the majority of the long Vice City Easter egg in GTA 6 , they left the world through a portal back to the ‘80s. When they came back to present-day Leonida, the cops didn’t care about them or their Tommy Vercetti shirt anymore. Here’s that clip: 世界初？GTA6で手配度6から逃げきることに成功しました https://t.co/0g7pSPJ6UU — ハイグレ玉夫 (@haiguretamao) November 24, 2026 “The cops in GTA are so overpowered that you can't escape them unless you go to another world,” said one commenter . “Now THAT'S how you escape the six star wanted level. That’s gangsta,” said another . One fan also claimed to have escaped six stars by swimming into an underwater research station. Unfortunately, the video doesn’t actually show the six stars vanishing, but I guess they technically escaped, as long as they stay there forever. 6 STARS ESCAPE Underwater Research Facility IN GTA 6 (is coded if you get 6 stars they will recognize you no matter what, testes same thing with 5 stars and it worked) https://t.co/jfZZMzdvs4 — fearcb (@Fearcbpr) November 23, 2026 It’ll be interesting to see if any new strategies formulate around losing six stars, although getting the full six isn’t something that generally happens by accident in ordinary gameplay. title: On Top of Everything Else, GTA 6 Is a Solid Stealth Sandbox
summary: I came to GTA 6 for its wild car chases and explosive shootouts, but its the really solid stealth that has me hooked.
content: This is an opinion piece from writer Samuel Horti. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games. Grand Theft Auto is a boisterous, brash series full of loud characters and louder explosions. GTA 6 continues that tradition for many of its main story beats, chaining showy set-pieces into lethal car chases, but in my 35 hours roaming Leonda I've found plenty of chances to engage with its surprisingly robust stealth system. In some cases, it even feels like Rockstar specifically designed areas with sneaking and silencers in mind. Illegal operations are lucrative robbery opportunities dotted around the map that hide cash, jewellery, drugs, and unique items – cars, weapons, watches – guarded by armies of enemies. I struggled with them early on: shooting my way to the valuables attracted GTA 6's menacing police, curtailing my heists before I could grab all the loot and forcing me to flee across entire counties while a chopper buzzed overhead. Now, I treat these scenarios like stealth vignettes, my goal to remain hidden for as long as possible. I've screwed silencers onto my weapons and prioritized headshot precision over spraying power, carrying a pistol alongside either a tactical rifle or a sniper. My shotgun is purely for backup, just in case. Skirting around these hideouts reveals hidden entrances. For Janjak's Garage in Vice City, for example, you can mantle a dumpster in a neighbouring alley to reach the garage's sheet metal roof. Out West, on the edge of Port Gellhorn, you can avoid the main gates of the giant Brooks Boatworks and slip through holes in the fence. Stealth detection is intuitive. Crouching reduces noise, sightlines feel realistic, and you'll be warned by a yellow arrow over an enemy's head before they fully spot you, allowing you a window to nip back into cover. Knives silently slice enemies' open or you can choke them quietly from behind. And if you need space, you can whistle from cover to draw foes over, or throw bottles to distract them. It's classic stealth game fare. But I've found that guns with silencers are actually the best option because they avoid the risk of an enemy spinning around at the wrong moment and catching you, knife raised. They mask shots almost completely: I've stood close to enemies and shot at others without being detected. Not everything in GTA 6 adopts Rockstar's general pursuit of realism. Illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. Clusters of enemies are tricky because as soon as you shoot one, the others will spin and look for you. Here, I use focus mode to slow time and pop a series of headshots, plink, plink, plink. Three bodies thud simultaneously. I feel like prime Sam Fisher. High ground is vital and from the right vantage I can survey the area, plan my route, and pick off enemies from distance. I always clamber to the loftiest point and use the D-pad to tag visible hostiles, which tracks them through walls. In a pinch, focus mode will highlight enemies through walls too, although only if they're nearby. Some of the level design feels like it's steering you down this silent route. Back at the Boatworks, the first thing I saw after sneaking in was a platform lift to the roof of the main warehouse, high above every enemy. A drop in the ceiling led me to an empty top floor – I've seen this trick repeated in other hideouts, so I always look for ladders or other ways to reach the roof. In the bigger compounds, staying silent for longer than a few minutes is a real challenge. No matter how many times I ran the Boatworks (I saved before I tried, and reloaded when I failed) I was always eventually spotted by some unaccounted-for enemy. But I reached a point where I could reliably clear the main warehouse floor-by-floor and empty the safe without anyone spotting me. That gave me a headstart on the police when I was eventually found, and by the time officers arrived I'd slipped back out through the fence, goodies jingling in my stash bag. This feels like the first time stealth has been a core part of a GTA game. During standard stick-ups of stores and jewellers you can find back entrances, kill the alarm and erase security tapes – but you'll always need to confront staff if you want to grab absolutely everything. For that reason, illegal operations feel like the real test of your sneakiness, and I'm relishing each new one that pops up on my map. They have the feel of Far Cry's outposts: flexible, self-contained diversions that I can tick off whenever I need more cash, or just fancy a change of pace. I've loved all my time with GTA 6 so far, but the best I've felt is when, this morning, I robbed Sound4Sound Studio in north Vice City. After hopping the fence I systematically cleared the parking lot and slipped inside, carving through the building, headshot after headshot. Nobody saw me coming, the police never arrived, and afterwards I could explore unchallenged, helping myself to every last bundle of cash. I drove off in a unique custom car, orange paint glistening, tens of thousands of dollars to the good. I'd take a whole game of these scenarios. Thankfully, I've still got 30 left. One final bonus of stealth: silencers are comically long, so now Lucia walks around Vice City carrying a gun taller than she is. title: Rockstar North Boss Knew Some GTA 6 Players Would 'Reject' New Systems Like Criminal Profiles, but Insists 'You Can Still Do Whatever You Wanted to Do Before'
summary: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson knew some GTA 6 players would "reject" new systems like criminal profiles, but insisted "you can still do whatever you wanted to do before."
content: GTA 6 is by far the furthest Rockstar has pushed one of its games on a gameplay level. Perhaps nothing showcases that more than the criminal profile system ticking away in the background at all times, judging the way you act in its world as Jason and Lucia. No longer is Grand Theft Auto a sandbox where hedonism is widely encouraged, but a place that judges you for partaking in it. It’s a system that has caused much debate within the player base, with some feeling as if they’re being punished for how they traditionally played GTA games. It was something that Rockstar admitted to have been a little worried about when YouTuber TGG visited the studio months ago and claimed it was "going to change GTA." "I thought, 'Oh s**t, we’re in trouble,'" Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson told VGC . “But I said, 'It doesn’t change everything; it changes what GTA can be.' So for us, I think it opens a new range of choices and decisions for the player to make. You can still do whatever you wanted to do before, but now you have other options." Warning! Spoilers for GTA 6 follow. The criminal profile system reacts to how violently you choose to act throughout GTA 6’s open world and missions. Opt for headshot kills over debilitating kneecaps? You’ll move away from the "professional" end of the spectrum towards "psycho" and eventually "irredeemable." From experience, though, I can confirm that it takes quite the effort to reach that point on the scale after going on one murderous rampage after the next. Which criminal profile you land on by the end of Jason and Lucia’s story will factor into which ending you get, but for the most part, it’s not something that necessarily needs to be playing on your mind at all times. My characters were considered “professional” at the end of my playthrough, and, believe me, I spilt my fair share of blood along the way. Nelson appears to know that not all players will necessarily be on board with changes to the GTA formula like this, though, and expects some to "reject this new stuff we’re offering." He does hope it may help to make people think differently about how they approach Rockstar games in a post-Red Dead Redemption 2 world, though. "I hope it changes the way players who want to engage with it play the game," Nelson continued to tell VGC. "In GTA 5 you started with a bank robbery in North Yankton, and you’re murdering like 40 cops off the rip, and you’re setting these guys up as what they are. We were conscious of that. "Lucia takes the bullets out of the gun at the start of the game. She goes in, and it’s not like you can kill a bunch of people. So we wanted to start them off with a bit less baggage. They’re trying to make a go of this semi-legitimate life. When you pick up with Jason, he’s still a criminal; he’s still getting in trouble with Donnie and all that, but he’s sort of been living this relatively criminal-adjacent existence." Whether GTA 6 feels like "classic GTA" or not is certainly a conversation to be had, but there’s no denying that the opening hours of Rockstar’s latest connects you to its characters more convincingly than the series has done in the past. title: The New York Times Book of Puzzle Games Drops to a New Low Price
content: The official New York Times Games puzzle book has dropped to its lowest price ever on Amazon, now down to only $12.63. The book itself is a physical collection of some of the most popular NYT digital games you can play right now, including Wordle, Connections, and Spelling Bee. This discount arrives as a Lightning Deal in Amazon's official Black Friday sale , which has been . If you're looking for a good gift for the word puzzle-inclined, I highly recommend checking this one out. The New York Times Games side of the business has really exploded over the last few years, with more than 100 people on staff making it happen. And all of that passion for word games is reflected in this book, which combines traditional crosswords with modern games like Wordle. My wife bought this book for her parents about a month ago, so I can confirm that it is actually a really cool piece of physical media. What games are included? Wordle Connections NYT Mini Crosswords Spelling Bee Trivia If you already play New York Times Games digitally, you'll be happy to know that the digital games aren't exactly the same in print form. The book puts slight spins on games like Spelling Bee and Connections that are entertaining in their own right. It's a great take on the classic puzzle book formula that offers a refreshing analog alternative to otherwise digital games. The 2025 edition of Puzzle Mania! was released back in October of last year and was named a finalist in Barnes & Noble's book of the year awards. A second volume has yet to be announced, but fans of the book are expecting the 2026 edition to drop sometime before the holidays .
